The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

The Gate at Snail Height

Bella loved the gate the Chirps had dressed for Everybody Day. It wore a chain of daisies from post to post. She flew through with her tummy tickling the petals. “Your turn, Snail!” she called.

Snail put out one feeler. Then the other. Both disappeared behind a curtain of petals. “Beautiful from here,” he said. “Very, very close. And rather beautifully in my nose.”

“I’ll carry you over!” Bella said. She looked at Snail. Snail looked at Bella. He was small, but so was she. “I rather like arriving on my own foot,” he said.

Bella tucked in her wings and walked the way Snail walked. Well, nearly the way. She had to use two feet. The flowers brushed her eyes before she could even see the party path.

She climbed the left post and lifted one loop. The gap beneath it was lovely. Then she let go. Plop. A daisy sat down on her head.

Snail looked up. “You passed a peg on the way,” he said. Together they chose a loop and Bella caught it on the peg. The chain made an arch with its feet in the grass.

Snail slid through. Halfway along, he stopped. “Would you look at that!” From under the arch he could see the whole crooked roof. Bella walked beside him, letting her wings have the afternoon off.

Their paper leaf for the Welcome Tree showed a little arch. Bella held it at Snail’s height while he inspected the drawing. “Yes,” he said. “You’ve left just enough sky.”

Read together

What can you see when you get down to Snail’s height?
